title: Nearest smaller element → days until warmer → circular next greater
label: ag-multi
statement: Given an integer array, return for each position the **value of the nearest element to its left that is strictly smaller**, or `-1` if there is none.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe a stack that stays monotonic — popping everything that can never be an answer again — gives every element its nearest smaller or greater neighbour in one O(n) pass, because each element is pushed and popped at most once. learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Given an integer array, return for each position the **value of the nearest element to its left that is strictly smaller**, or `-1` if there is none.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Strictly smaller, or smaller-or-equal? (Strictly.)
- Return values or indices? (Values here; Daily Temperatures returns distances.)
- What size — is O(n²) acceptable? (No; n up to 10^6.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Anything to the left that is >= the current value can never be the answer for any later element either — the current value is nearer and no larger. So pop it. What remains is a strictly increasing stack, and its top is the answer.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "A." stack that stays monotonic — popping everything that can never be an answer again — gives every element its nearest smaller or greater neighbour in one O(n) pass, because each element is pushed and popped at most once."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- The O(n²) double loop presented as fine.
- >= vs > in the pop condition (duplicates).
- Storing values when the follow-up needs indices (Daily Temperatures).
- Circular variant: pushing during the second pass, or looping n times instead of 2n.
